dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Hello, hello... Uh, I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Ahem. Happy Lantern Rite! May you stay healthy and hale, and may all go well with you!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Haha, I guess I've finally gotten used to the festive greetings that locals give one another...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Hello, hello. Oh, ah, I mean, good fortune! I'm still not accustomed to using the local greetings.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the letter to your family...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Ah, you've delivered it to my parents, have you? Thank you very much. It's a relief to know that they're doing well.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: My mother would most likely keep worrying, while my father would try to comfort her while keeping his own worries in his heart...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: *sigh* It was only after leaving that I realized how much they must miss. I'm... really sorry for making them worry.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About your homeland...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Sometimes I miss the sights that I used to see in my home... The tranquil Chinju Forest, the lovely Sacred Sakura... I grew up with them.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But after the Sakoku Decree was implemented, Inazuma really became such an oppressive place. For someone who loves freedom like me, it was simply unbearable.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: If we wanted to leave, we'd have to go through several stages of application and approval with the Kanjou Commission. Most people would never get the chance to see the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Perhaps the Shogunate really knows best in having such strict control, but the allure of the open sea and the freedom it represents grew inside me until I couldn't take it anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: That's why I eventually just grabbed the nearest vessel I could find and set out to sea.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: The journey was tough, but thanks to the intervention of some locals from Liyue, I now have my freedom!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Okay, stay safe!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: We meet again! It's great to see you here in Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hello there, Atsuko.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: It has been a long time, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Previously, we would only meet in Liyue Harbor. I never expected that I would run into you again here.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: It seems that you travel between nations quite frequently. That's very impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've returned home, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I heard from the Crux Fleet's sailors that the Almighty Shogun has abolished the Sakoku Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: So I thought to myself, maybe the samurai at the Police Station might give me a pass and let me return home.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: So I boarded a ship bound for Inazuma. I found upon my return that many things have changed.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But the biggest change was... Well, my parents had aged a lot. They had been concerned for my safety this whole time...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Still, they were all smiles when they greeted me. That was something that didn't change.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: That's why I've decided to stay for a while longer to accompany them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Goodbye. Safe travels.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you heard about that other "you"?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Oh? You mean the one who was staying with my parents at one point?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Um, how should I put it... It's such a strange story...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: That said, I'd love to meet "her" if I have the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Who knows, "she" might be able to help me out a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still want to travel the world?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Haha, you remember that? Thanks for the concern.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I'm still serious about that dream. I'm sure you understand me as only a fellow traveler could.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Now that Inazuma's policies have changed so much, going out to travel is no longer such an arduous task... So if a suitable opportunity comes along, I'll continue my journey.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But for now, I'll continue to stay with my parents.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's not great, surely...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: What's wrong with it? You mean, breaking Inazuman regulations?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I think it depends on the person. Some people are quite content to spend their whole lives within the fences of their farm...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But not me! If there's anything that can fence me in, it's somewhere beyond these lands, beyond the seas, beyond the stars!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: If you can't understand the value of freedom, let me be the one to explain it to you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Freedom...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Perhaps everyone has a different understanding of and way of pursuing freedom...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Some people are quite content to spend their whole lives within the fences of their farm...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: But not me! If there's anything that can fence me in, it's somewhere beyond these lands, beyond the seas, beyond the stars!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Only by breaking through these boundaries and going out into the world can we understand the value of freedom!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I wish you the best of luck.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Though this has been quite the bumpy ride, it does not seem so hard while freedom yet stirs in my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I hope that your future journeys will go smoothly as well!

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I wonder how mom is doing, and dad as well...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Oh? Traveler? What are you doing here? I remember you asked me how to go to Inazuma last time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've been to Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: You did go. And you managed to come back...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: You live up to your reputation as a warrior. Your abilities are far beyond those of ordinary folks like me.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Oh right! If you don't mind, can you do me a favor?

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: When I left Inazuma, I left without saying goodbye.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: Ever since I was little, I've longed for the world outside of Inazuma. I liked to travel and I disliked being controlled by my parents.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: After they issued the Vision Hunt Decree, the atmosphere in Inazuma has become increasingly suffocating. That's why I decided to leave my hometown.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: When I came to Liyue, although I managed to find a way to survive. I couldn't find a reliable person to send a message to my family back home.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: Can I ask you for a favor to help deliver a letter to my parents?

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: Thank you! Well, I'll leave the letter to you.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: By the way, my father's name is "Yoh," and my mother's name is "Michiru." I'll mark the address on the map for you.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: After leaving my hometown, I've experienced a lot. Now I know that if I want to become an independent and strong woman, I can't just rely on my parents like before.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I've decided that I won't go back to my hometown in the near future. If I encounter any difficulties outside, I will face them by myself.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I think my parents will be proud of me if I can do that.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I also wrote about my determination in the letter, so please take it to my parents.

choices.text: Do you want to go back and have a look?

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: Although I miss my parents, if I go back now, I'm afraid I won't be able to leave anymore.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I don't have the ability to come and go freely like you. No matter what, I wouldn't dare to go back.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I'll be happy if you can take this letter to Inazuma. I really wouldn't ask for anything more.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I wonder how mom is doing, and dad as well...

choices.text: Do you want to go back and have a look?

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I miss my parents, that's true, but there are still things that I need to do here in Liyue...

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I don't have the ability to come and go freely like you, either, so though I'd love to return, I can't.

response.speaker: Atsuko
response.text: I'll be happy if you can take this letter to Inazuma. As for what comes after... we can talk about it afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Hello, hello. Oh, ah, I mean, good fortune! I'm still not accustomed to using the local greetings.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are...?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm so sorry, my name is Atsuko, it's lovely to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: I've never seen this many outlanders before back in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hi there! You don't seem to be from around here either.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: That's right, I'm from Inazuma. It's been a long road getting here.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Facing the crashing waves before me, whilst trying to escape the forces behind me... My raft sank, my money got swept away by the sea...

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Was a good thing the locals helped me, otherwise I wouldn't be standing here today. I've decided I want to get a job on a boat and travel all around the world.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Okay, stay safe!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Yes, my home, back on the other side of the ocean.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Though I don't wish to speak ill of my homeland, the pressure back home is just too much.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: If you want to leave, you have to go through several stages of application and approval with the Kanjou Commission. Most people never get the chance to see the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: Perhaps the Shogunate really knows best in having such strict control, but the allure of the open sea and the freedom it represents grew inside me until I couldn't take it anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: So... One day when I was gazing out to see, something in me just snapped. I just took the nearest vessel I could find and set out to sea.

dialogues.speaker: Atsuko
dialogues.text: So if you see anyone wearing clothes similar to mine, they're probably from Inazuma. Please, if you see such a person, you cannot breathe a word of this to them, they cannot know I'm here. Please, I beg of you.
